title: Varro agriculture task-state constructor with worker/tool ownership
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Varro De re rustica I opens a complete agricultural planning dialogue and distinguishes the work's land, season, tools, workers, crop arrangement and profit conditions. A task-state constructor keeps one farm identity while changing operation ownership and timing; a static crop list is the rival.

source.work: Varro, De re rustica, Book I
source.source_span: I.1–2 programme and interlocutors; I.8–11 agricultural domains and aids; I.32 cultivation form/quincunx example
source_facts: Varro announces separate books for agriculture, animal husbandry, and the steading, and identifies which subjects belong to agriculture proper.
The dialogue assigns questions to people with different practical expertise and lists aids such as land, tools, labour and timing.
I.32 discusses orchard arrangement in regular quincunx rows and connects cultivation form with profit rather than treating plant names as isolated labels.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Varro agriculture/task state and route-check cultivation/graft/recipe; Cato133 and Palladius graft cards excluded
duplicate_screen.difference: The proposed mechanism is dialogue-owned task/worker/tool scope and profit consequence, not Cato's attached scion state, graft direction, or a preparation branch.

worked_examples: same named crop under a different task owner/tool or domain shifts the result; moving the task into animal husbandry changes scope rather than plant identity
constructor.consequence: A shared farm identity can carry different task domains and operators while the layout/worker/tool state changes the profit consequence. A static catalogue predicts no difference between the same crop under different task ownership or timing.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete agricultural passages sharing a farm/material referent but changing task domain or operator owner, with a downstream profit/cultivation consequence.
constructor.rival: The dialogue is a list of crop facts; speaker, tool, season and domain headings are metadata with no semantic effect.
assumptions: The dialogue's expertise assignments are treated as typed task ownership.
Profit is retained as a source claim, not measured or modernized.
failure_modes: Varro's opening programme may be expository rather than an operational farm record.
The quincunx example does not quantify profit, so output is qualitative.
No target binding for worker, farm or season exists.

dependencies: Source-owned dialogue and cultivation example; no target page or crop label is consulted.
access: Source-only; no target, reserve, image, experiment, route, ledger, decoder, or root file access.
